sourcedFrom: Ruger AR-556 Autoloading Rifle Instruction Manual — PM263 (2018)
cleanIntro: Ruger’s own field strip for the AR-556: selector safe, rear takedown pin from the left, hinge it open, carrier and charging handle out.

steps.title: Clear it and set the selector to SAFE
steps.action: Clear the chamber, hold the pistol grip, and switch the selector to the "SAFE" position. Then press the upper thumb pad of the bolt catch to release the bolt carrier into battery.
steps.prose: Selector to SAFE before anything moves. The bolt goes forward under control, not by slipping off the catch.
steps.cite: Ruger AR-556 Autoloading Rifle Instruction Manual — PM263 — Disassembly, step 2, p.25
steps.warn: Always unload a firearm before cleaning, lubrication, disassembly, or assembly.

steps.title: Push the rear takedown pin from the left
steps.action: On the left-hand side of the lower receiver, push the rear takedown pin to the right.
steps.prose: If it is stiff, Ruger permits a punch and a gentle tap with a hammer — and notes it loosens with use. Do not lever it.
steps.quote: On the left-hand side of the lower receiver, push the rear takedown pin to the right.
steps.cite: Ruger AR-556 Autoloading Rifle Instruction Manual — PM263 — Disassembly, step 3a, p.25

steps.title: Pull it to the detent stop — and hold the receivers
steps.action: From the right side, pull the pin outward until the detent stops any further travel. Hold the upper and lower together until you are ready to open the rifle.
steps.prose: Ruger’s warning here is specific to this rifle: once the pin is out the upper moves FORWARD, and fingers around the magazine well are what get pinched.
steps.caution: The upper receiver will move forward once the pin is disengaged and could pinch your fingers if you are holding the magazine well.
steps.quote: From the right side of the rifle, pull the pin outward until the detent stops any additional travel.
steps.cite: Ruger AR-556 Autoloading Rifle Instruction Manual — PM263 — Disassembly, step 3b, p.25
steps.warn: The upper receiver will move forward once the pin is disengaged and could pinch your fingers if you are holding the magazine well.

steps.title: Open it on the front pivot pin
steps.action: Tip the upper receiver forward on the front pivot pin to reach the bolt carrier assembly and charging handle.
steps.prose: The front pin stays in — the rifle hinges open on it.
steps.quote: Tip the upper receiver forward on the front pivot pin to access the carrier assembly and charging handle.
steps.cite: Ruger AR-556 Autoloading Rifle Instruction Manual — PM263 — Disassembly, step 4a, p.25

steps.title: Charging handle and carrier out together
steps.action: Unlock the charging handle by holding it with index and middle fingers and pulling it away while compressing the latch, then draw it about halfway out and stop — the carrier assembly follows it.
steps.prose: Halfway and stop. Pulling the handle all the way first leaves the carrier stranded.
steps.quote: Pull the charging handle about halfway out and stop. The carrier assembly will follow the charging handle.
steps.cite: Ruger AR-556 Autoloading Rifle Instruction Manual — PM263 — Disassembly, step 4c, p.25

steps.title: Carrier off, then the handle
steps.action: Grasp the back of the carrier assembly, remove it from the upper receiver and set it aside, then withdraw the charging handle.
steps.prose: That is the field strip — upper, lower, carrier group, charging handle.
steps.quote: Grasp the backside of the carrier assembly and remove it from upper receiver and set aside.
steps.cite: Ruger AR-556 Autoloading Rifle Instruction Manual — PM263 — Disassembly, step 4d, p.25

deepAbsentReason: PM263 documents the field strip — takedown pin, upper open, carrier group and charging handle out. It publishes no disassembly past that point, so this listing has NO deep clean.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Solvent-wet patch from the chamber end, then a correctly sized brush, then dry patches until clean
Clean the chamber and locking lug recesses — carbon collects there first

cleaning.name: BOLT CARRIER GROUP
tasks: Scrub the bolt face and the extractor recess
Clean carbon off the bolt tail and the inside of the carrier
Wipe the gas rings and check they are not aligned to a single gap
Light oil on the carrier rails and the cam pin

cleaning.name: UPPER & LOWER
tasks: Wipe the upper receiver interior and the charging handle channel
Brush the lower receiver, especially around the trigger group
Keep oil light — an AR runs wet on the carrier, not in the fire control

reassembly: Return the charging handle to its channel, then the bolt carrier assembly, and seat both fully.
Close the upper onto the lower and push the rear takedown pin back through from the right.
Function-check with the magazine out and the chamber confirmed empty.
fncheck: With the magazine out and the chamber confirmed empty: selector to SAFE blocks the trigger, the bolt carrier runs freely, and the bolt catch holds it open.
